criteria.name: Hook strength
criteria.notes: Two short opening lines name Seely, ERCOT, and the anchor front of the line; unchanged from cycle 1, a plainer hook than a headline would be.

criteria.name: Subject and decision significance for Texas
criteria.notes: A grid-queue sequencing decision covering about 200 gigawatts of demand is consequential, but it is a process choice rather than a single headline decision.

criteria.name: Identity and decision fidelity
criteria.notes: Title from Utility Dive Aug 21, decision date Aug 20 from the ERCOT presentation, Tribune quote and dates match the dossier.

criteria.name: Source quality and independence
criteria.notes: Primary ERCOT presentation plus two independent outlets; the presentation does not name Seely, so individual ownership is carried by reporting of his statements.

criteria.name: Structural read
criteria.notes: Cycle 2 edit: explains the classification mechanism, the alternative ERCOT declined, and the verification gate before studies, all sourced in the ERCOT record.

criteria.name: Concrete next check
criteria.notes: Names the December 10th, 2026 verification report and the disqualification criteria as the checkable item.

criteria.name: Texas AI Docket voice
criteria.notes: Neutral accountability voice, no first person, no advocacy, no rating.

criteria.name: LinkedIn readability
criteria.notes: Short paragraphs, 408 body words, within the 3000 character cap.

criteria.name: Specific engagement question
criteria.notes: Cycle 2 edit: asks whether the December filing names the disqualification criteria so a developer can check its own load.

criteria.name: Credibility and proportionality
criteria.notes: Claims stay within fetched statements; the ownership caveat is stated in the dossier and not overstated in the post.

cycle_note: Cycle 1 recomputed 7.915, below threshold. Cycle 2 made two real edits (structural mechanism sentence, specific closing question) and re-scored; the hook score was not changed.
